paragraphs.heading: Why naturalism can't account for agency
paragraphs.edited: Why can't naturalism account for agency? Think about it. On naturalism there is no immaterial soul. There's no self distinct from nature that can make meaningful, genuinely free choices. Although humans are more complex, ultimately they are a purely physical object, like water. When water is poured into a glass, what happens? Does it consider its options? Does it decide its shape or temperature? Of course not. Because of the laws of nature and the molecular structure of water, it will fit to the shape of the glass. In naturalism, we human beings are like this water: purely physical objects whose behavior and beliefs and actions simply conform to the physical structure around us. There is no agency. There are no genuine choices that we make as persons.

paragraphs.heading: Sam Harris writes a book
paragraphs.edited: In fact, this is why many atheists will recognize and admit that if atheism is true, agency is out the window. Sam Harris, one of the most well-known atheists today, in his book titled Free Will, says, quote, free will is an illusion. I have to wonder, why did Harris even bother to write the book? After all, when you write a book, you think that you're writing down ideas that are genuinely up to you, and the goal is to persuade other people, other agents, to adopt your viewpoints. The very point of writing a book assumes that people can be persuaded freely by your ideas. And yet the premise of his entire book is that we don't have free will, that we're not genuinely free agents. So again, his worldview says we are not agents, but his actions portray and reveal his true beliefs.

paragraphs.heading: Monotheism accounts for agency
paragraphs.edited: Of all the worldviews, monotheism best accounts for agency. The world is, after all, the free creation of a personal agent, God, and we have been made in his image and given the responsibility and ability to make choices. We are not simply part of nature. We are agents who make meaningful choices within nature.

paragraphs.heading: Great power, great responsibility
paragraphs.edited: My favorite superhero by far is Spider-Man, also known as Peter Parker. His uncle, Ben Parker, once said to him, with great power comes great responsibility. As human beings we have been given great power. We have the ability to make meaningful choices that deeply affect the world that we live in, and with that great power does come great responsibility. We have responsibility to one another as human beings, and if there is a divine agent, God, we just might have responsibility to him too.
